note: Cross-platform known answers for Hubs private conversations (end-to-end encrypted DMs). Every key is a test key made for these vectors and used nowhere real. Bytes are hex unless a field says otherwise; the wire carries the same bytes as standard base64. Generated by our vector generator with fixed inputs and seeded randomness, and checked by typescript/test/e2ee-vectors.test.ts and rust/hubs-mls/tests/e2ee_vectors.rs. Steps run in order: a native client replays them as the receivers named and must reach the same plaintexts and refuse every refusal. The protocol a client must follow is in docs/protocol.md.

deviceRemoval.note: A device removes a member the server stopped listing only when removalCounts says so. Bytes are Ed25519 signatures over the bodies (raw signature, not MLS SignWithLabel); at is milliseconds in decimal.

signedRemovalsNote.note: A commit's authenticated data once the sender's account has made the statement: the fixed label, then the statement's 64-byte signature. readSignedRemovalsNote returns that signature, and null for anything else, including an empty value or a 32-byte franking commitment.

backupCounter.note: A backup bundle carries counter, one more than any backup the saving device knew of; a link bundle carries backupCounter, the highest the old device has seen. A device refuses a backup whose counter (0 when missing) is below the highest it has seen. The server stores the counter in the clear beside the sealed copy and refuses an upload whose counter is not above the stored one.

missingMessages.note: Per epoch and sender leaf, other people only, from the first epoch the device followed from its start (it joined with a welcome, created the group, or accepted or made a commit). graceMs is how long a gap stays open before one notice tells it. A late arrival of a told generation settles that notice. Generations come from the MLS sender data (RFC 9420 section 6.3.2).

lastResort.note: Bob's last-resort key package, handed out only when his one-time ones run out. Two conversations add him with it; he joins both with the same private half, which he keeps until the package expires plus the 30-day queue. On the server the package carries lastResort and is never deleted on claim.

generations.note: Alice adds Bob and sends three messages in one epoch. Bob reads each message's sender leaf and generation from the sender data, before or without opening the content.

calls.note: Calls, protocol 3 (src/calls.ts in the private messages package). P-256 keys are fixed scalars (connectionScalarHex); public keys are 65 uncompressed bytes. Every Ed25519 signature is deterministic. A native client must build every body byte for byte, open every wrap and refuse every one listed under mustNotOpen, refuse every binding under refusedBindings, make every code, verify the roster statement, and reach the same decision for every policy case, in order for policyLists.
